user_saw: A Codex-backed chat could fail to continue after compaction because the previous app-server process still held the thread’s writer lock.
summary: The fix makes compaction reuse the recorded writer when possible and blocks replacement writers until the retiring process exits.
reasoning: The July 1 snapshot already shows compaction acquiring a generic shared client and releasing its lease without waiting for process exit. I checked the later client-acquisition and thread-queue changes, but found no verified transition from a working handoff to a broken one, and the offline path history stopped at the shallow boundary before I could identify the introducing commit.
